notes: OpenSearch connection pool exhaustion fix — mirrors Neptune fix from commit 6ad5094

completedSteps.name: Research — Audit OpenSearch connection lifecycle
completedSteps.notes: Four leak points identified: OpenSearchAdapter unbounded socket pool, close() no-op, entrypoint missing SIGTERM handler, kiro-proxy missing stop_runtime_session. Parity test already compliant from Neptune fix 6ad5094.

completedSteps.name: Add HTTP agent configuration to OpenSearchAdapter
completedSteps.notes: Added node:https Agent import, poolConfig (maxSockets:10, maxFreeSockets:5, keepAliveMsecs:30000, socketTimeout:60000). connect() now creates bounded HTTPS agent; close() properly calls client.close() and agent.destroy().

completedSteps.name: Add SIGTERM/SIGINT graceful shutdown to mcp-agentcore-entrypoint.js
completedSteps.notes: Added gracefulShutdown(signal) with 5s timeout guard. Closes HTTP server then calls sharedDataAccess.close() which releases NeptuneAdapter.driver + OpenSearchAdapter agent/client.

completedSteps.name: Add connection cleanup to test scripts
completedSteps.notes: mcp-parity-test.py already compliant. Extended scope: added AgentCoreClient.stop_session() to tools/agentcore-kiro-proxy.py and wrapped main loop in try/finally so session is released on any exit path.

completedSteps.name: Baseline capture; full validation deferred to post-deploy
completedSteps.notes: CloudWatch ActiveConnectionCount is not exposed for managed OpenSearch — confirmed via list-metrics. Baseline captured (OpenSearchRequests 1-13/hr typical with 147 peak; 5xx=0). Full validation against the fix requires v8 deployed (Step 7). Acceptance re-interpreted as application-level: absence of 'Max connection limit reached' from get_knowledge_base_status.
